reasons: Classification is correct: a 180-day non-renewal notice window is double the 90-day walk-away threshold and triple the 60-day fallback, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term and is a genuine deviation.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a targeted edit — notice window cut to 30 days, successive twelve-month terms preserved (no multi-year auto-renewal introduced), and a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder added; the deterministic notice-window check confirms 30 days.
The high changed-character ratio (0.669) is an artifact of a short one-sentence clause plus the added reminder sentence; no unnecessary substantive changes were introduced.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and correctly offers the 60-day fallback.

Rationale properly notes that Section 8.3 already meets the preferred pricing position, avoiding double-flagging the same commercial term, and folds the minor missing reminder mechanic into the same edit rather than raising it separately.
